messages:
Jordan Anders: Hi team — my oldest child just turned 26 last week. How do I remove them from medical/dental benefits and what's the cutoff date? The portal is throwing an error when I try to remove dependent 😕
Maya (People Ops): @Jordan sorry for the hassle. When a dependent ages out at 26 our plan ends at the end of the month of their 26th birthday unless there's qualifying event exceptions. Can you confirm DOB and whether they have alternative coverage?
Jordan Anders: DOB 1999-03-10 (turned 26 on 2025-03-10). They have an employer plan starting 4/1. I tried removing via benefits.redwood.com -> Dependent > Remove and it fails with "Unable to process request".
benefits-bot: Automated note: Portal maintenance window 2025-03-12 02:00-03:00 UTC (should be complete). If issue persists, contact benefits team.
Maya (People Ops): Thanks. Since the new employer coverage starts 4/1, we should set the dependent removal effective 3/31/2025. We need proof of the dependent's DOB (birth certificate or passport) and proof of other coverage (offer letter/ID card) to process the change and COBRA eligibility notice.
Priya (Benefits): Adding: COBRA is only for group plans when dependent loses eligibility — but COBRA is typically for the covered employee and dependents; in this case the dependent may be offered continuation by their own employer, so COBRA from our side isn't applicable. We'll send an endpoint notice about loss of eligibility per ERISA rules.
Jordan Anders: Got it. Where do I upload docs? Is there a form? Also any refund of premiums for April deductions?
Sam (HR Intern): You can upload to the secure portal under MyClaims -> Dependent Changes. Quick path: https://benefits.redwood.com/upload (sso required). File name recommended: jordan_dep_removal_2025-03.pdf. If portal still errors, DM me and I can upload on your behalf.
Alex (Payroll): Payroll note: If the removal effective date is 3/31, April premiums should not be deducted for the dependent starting in the 4/1 payroll cycle. If premiums for April have already been taken, payroll can issue an adjustment in the next payroll run once benefits confirms the effective date. Typical timeline: 1 pay cycle to process.
Jordan Anders: I checked; April deductions hit this morning. If I upload proof now, how long until I see the refund?
Priya (Benefits): Once we receive docs we verify within 2 business days. Then we update the enrollment system and notify payroll. Refund/adjustment usually posts in 1-2 pay cycles after payroll receives the enrollment change. We'll CC you on the ticket.
Jordan Anders: Uploaded birth_cert.pdf and new_employer_evidence.pdf to portal (both uploaded at 2025-03-15 09:12). Please confirm.
Maya (People Ops): Confirmed receipt. We filed the dependent removal with effective date 2025-03-31 and flagged for payroll adjustment.
Alex (Payroll): Got the update from benefits. We will process an off-cycle adjustment if needed; otherwise it will be included in the next pay run. I will DM @Jordan expected amount once calculated.
Priya (Benefits): Also sending the ERISA notice to the dependent's email on file about loss of eligibility and options.
Jordan Anders: Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround. One more Q: do I need to complete any COBRA forms for myself?
Priya (Benefits): No action required for you unless your own eligibility changes. This is only a dependent termination due to aging out. If anything else changes we'll reach out.
Maya (People Ops): Marking this thread resolved. @Jordan if you don't see the payroll adjustment in two cycles ping us and we'll escalate. :thumbsup:
Jordan Anders: Will do, thanks everyone! :relieved:
